column3: Fan-out input shadowed in an inner scope
column4: Both branches call `.run`/`.apply` with an argument spelled like the arrow's input, but the second resolves to a different binding, so under `&&&` the two Kleislis would no longer run on the same input.
column5: Rename the inner binding so it no longer shadows the arrow's input, or pass the input explicitly; then re-run `<module>.fix`.

column3: Kleisli body declined by the readability budget
column4: The body could be written point-free, but the rendered composition would read worse than the hand-threaded original, so the rule declined.
column5: Leave the body as it is, or split it into named Kleislis whose composition stays readable; re-run `<module>.fix` to see whether the rule now rewrites it.

column3: Kleisli body the parser did not recognise
column4: The body has no monadic spine the Arrow parser understands, so no point-free form was attempted; this is reported only under `PreferArrow.reportSkips`.
column5: Compare the reported shape with the recognised entries in docs/ARROW_PATTERNS.md and restructure the body into a `for`/`flatMap` spine over the input, or leave it and turn `reportSkips` off.

column3: Body matches more than one Cats function
column4: The normalized body matches more than one public Cats function and ranking (public > in-scope > shortest) did not resolve a unique winner, so the rule did not rewrite.
column5: Pick the Cats function you mean and call it directly, or narrow the body so only one matches; see docs/PREFER_CATS_FUNCTIONS.md §3-4 (D1), then compile.

column3: Cats match needs typeclass evidence not in scope
column4: The matching Cats function requires a typeclass constraint that is not derivable from the enclosing parameter list, so the rewrite would not compile.
column5: Add the required typeclass constraint (for example a context bound) to the enclosing definition and re-run `<module>.fix`; see docs/PREFER_CATS_FUNCTIONS.md §3 (D3).

column3: Body matches only a private Cats symbol
column4: The body matches only a private or internal Cats implementation detail with no public API of the same normalized shape, and the rule never rewrites to a non-public symbol.
column5: Keep the body, or express it through a public Cats function; see docs/PREFER_CATS_FUNCTIONS.md §3 (D2).

column3: Manual acquire/release in try/finally
column4: A `finally` that closes a resource and does something else too cannot have the close lifted out mechanically, so the acquire/release stays invisible to the effect system.
column5: Reduce the `finally` to the close alone so `Using.resource` applies, or move the body into `F` and wrap it in `Resource.make(acquire)(release)`; run `<module>.fix` again and compile.

column3: AtomicReference in effectful code
column4: An `AtomicReference` threading state through an effectful body is a `cats.effect.Ref` in disguise, and rewriting it means lifting every use into `F`.
column5: Replace the `AtomicReference` with a `Ref[F, A]` created once in the resource scope and update it through `Ref.update`/`modify`; then compile.

column3: Unchecked asInstanceOf
column4: An `asInstanceOf` is a claim the compiler cannot check, so a wrong one fails at runtime instead of at compile time.
column5: Model the case in the type or pattern match on it, then compile to confirm the cast is gone.

column3: Lookup that throws on a missing key
column4: `getOrElse(key, throw ...)` is a partial lookup wearing a total signature, so the caller cannot see that the key may be absent.
column5: Return `Option` from the lookup and let the caller decide what a missing key means; then compile and fix the call sites.

column3: Container does not stay abstract
column4: An operation on the container is not covered by the solved constraints, or its value is passed to a signature that names a concrete container, so the widened body would not compile.
column5: Widen the receiving signature too, or replace the uncovered operation with one the constraint provides; then re-run `<module>.fix`.

column3: Container def called with explicit type arguments
column4: A call site names this def's type arguments and inference cannot replace them, so the def cannot take another type parameter.
column5: Let the call sites infer the type arguments, or leave the signature concrete; then re-run `<module>.fix`.

column3: Container def handed over as a value
column4: The def is referenced as a value rather than called, and a polymorphic method has no monomorphic function type, so widening it would stop that reference compiling.
column5: Call the def at the use site instead of passing it as a value, or leave the signature concrete.

column3: No free type parameter name
column4: Every candidate name for the new type parameter (`S`, `C`, `G`) is already taken in the definition, so the rule has nothing to introduce.
column5: Rename one of the existing type parameters to free a candidate name, then re-run `<module>.fix`.

column3: No Cats capability covers the container's use
column4: No Cats typeclass in the index covers how the body uses the container, so there is no weaker signature to widen to.
column5: Keep the concrete collection, or rewrite the body in terms of `Foldable`/`Functor`/`Traverse` operations and re-run `<module>.fix`.

column3: Container used by position
column4: The body reaches an element by position or order -- `xs(i)`, `.indices`, `.head`, `.sorted` -- which expresses random access, and Cats has no typeclass for that.
column5: Express the body through `Foldable`/`Traverse` operations (`foldLeft`, `get`, `traverse`) or keep the concrete collection.

column3: Container abstractable but rewriting is off
column4: The container is abstractable over the reported constraints, but `PreferPolymorphicCollections.rewrite = false` leaves the signature unchanged.
column5: Widen the signature by hand to `S[_]` with the reported constraints, or set `rewrite = true` and re-run `<module>.fix`.

column3: Widening needs too many constraints
column4: Widening the container needs more typeclass constraints than `maxConstraints` allows, so the signature would be busier than the concrete one.
column5: Raise `PreferPolymorphicCollections.maxConstraints`, or split the body so each def needs fewer capabilities; then re-run `<module>.fix`.

column3: Unsupported type-constructor kind
column4: The container's type constructor has a kind the rule does not abstract over, such as the binary `Map[K, V]`.
column5: Keep the concrete type, or widen only the unary containers in the signature.

column3: Operations with unrelated capability roots
column4: The body uses operations whose Cats capabilities have unrelated roots, so no single weakest typeclass covers them.
column5: Split the body so each def needs one capability family, or keep the concrete type.

column3: Pattern match on a concrete constructor
column4: The body matches on the constructor's own cases, such as `Nil` or `Some`, which fixes the concrete type and cannot be expressed through a typeclass.
column5: Replace the match with a `fold`-style operation from the typeclass, or keep the concrete type.

column3: Def called with explicit type arguments
column4: A call site names this def's type arguments and inference cannot replace them, so the def cannot take another type parameter.
column5: Let the call sites infer the type arguments, or leave the signature concrete; then re-run `<module>.fix`.

column3: Def handed over as a value
column4: The def is referenced as a value rather than called, and a polymorphic method has no monomorphic function type, so widening it would stop that reference compiling.
column5: Call the def at the use site instead of passing it as a value, or leave the signature concrete.

column3: No free type parameter name
column4: Every candidate name for the new type parameter (`G`, `H`, `K`) is already taken in the definition, so the rule has nothing to introduce.
column5: Rename one of the existing type parameters to free a candidate name, then re-run `<module>.fix`.

column3: Constructor used by position
column4: The body reaches an element by position or order -- `xs(i)`, `.indices`, `.head`, `.sorted` -- which expresses random access, and Cats has no typeclass for that.
column5: Express the body through `Foldable`/`Traverse` operations (`foldLeft`, `get`, `traverse`) or keep the concrete type.

column3: Constructor abstractable but rewriting is off
column4: The type constructor is abstractable over the reported constraints, but `PreferPolymorphicTypeclasses.rewrite = false` leaves the signature unchanged.
column5: Widen the signature by hand to `G[_]` with the reported constraints, or set `rewrite = true` and re-run `<module>.fix`.

column3: Public API boundary kept concrete
column4: The def is public and `PreferPolymorphicTypeclasses.widenPublic = false`, so its signature is a boundary the rule does not change.
column5: Make the def private, or set `widenPublic = true` if the call sites can absorb the new type parameter; then re-run `<module>.fix`.

column3: Body the widening cannot carry
column4: The body throws, returns early, mutates a variable, or calls a method with no typeclass counterpart, so the constructor cannot be abstracted.
column5: Remove the obstacle -- return a value instead of throwing or mutating, or replace the call -- and re-run `<module>.fix`.

column3: Merge point outside the closure
column4: A node the closure reached also receives a value the closure does not cover, so it keeps the underlying type and the call site unwraps.
column5: Add the reported symbol to `widen` if that value belongs in the conversion too, otherwise leave the merge point unwrapped; then re-run `<module>.fix`.

column3: SemanticDB out of date
column4: The SemanticDB payload for this file no longer matches the source on disk, so a closure computed from it would be wrong and the file was left unchanged.
column5: Recompile to regenerate SemanticDB and re-run `<module>.fix`.

column3: Side effect the signature does not mention
column4: A method whose declared result is not an effect but whose body touches the world runs the effect when it is called, so nothing can sequence, retry or defer it.
column5: Move the method to `F[A]` under `Sync` and wrap the body in `Sync[F].delay`, or mark a realtime path with `// purrism:keep <reason>`; then update the call sites and compile.
